meta.source: 2026 Scout manual table of contents and section text (Parts 1 to 5); Navigator and Ranger manuals use the same parts
meta.note: A locator, not a standard. Each row is this project's reading of what a manual section asks students to do; the skills shown are those of the competencies listed. Props and Leadership are added here: Props is a subsection of Part 1, and Leadership is not a section at all. Which items count, and the points, differ by class and year; check the current manual.

rows.asks: Each year's real-world science story behind the missions.
The client's requirements, point values and limits for the mission.
The underwater jobs the vehicle must do.
A device that sinks, rises and reports on its own.
Building the mission props to practice on.
The inspection every vehicle passes, with a system interconnection diagram.
Size, weight, sealing, propellers and how the vehicle is launched.

rows.section: 3.3 Electrical, 3.4 Onboard power and 3.5 Power shutdown
rows.asks: Fuses, wiring, power limits and the shutdown switch.
Hydraulics and pneumatics, with limits and a diagram.
How the pilot drives and sees, and how the tether is built.
What is allowed and what it takes to use one safely.
Roles at the pool, timing and how the run is scored.
Pool safety, wireless interference and building for the real venue.
A one-page snapshot of the company and its vehicle.
The engineering notebook or report: design choices, tests, troubleshooting.
Explaining the design to judges and answering their questions.
Telling a non-technical audience what the company does.
Education, community engagement and measurable impact.

rows.section: Tips for written and oral communication
rows.asks: How to tell the engineering story, compare options and record decisions.

rows.section: 6.1 Required documents (SID, tech documentation, spec sheet)
rows.asks: What to submit and bring.
Due dates set by each regional.

rows.section: Start-up company roles (CEO, CFO, R&D, testing, operations, marketing)
rows.asks: Run the team as a company, with a person responsible for each job.

rows.section: Organizational and operational effectiveness (scored, Navigator and Ranger)
rows.asks: Show teamwork, communication, project management and problem solving across the whole project.

parts.name: Product Demonstration
parts.blurb: The year's science story, the client's request and the underwater tasks, including the profiling float.

parts.name: Vehicle Design and Building
parts.blurb: The safety inspection and the specifications for size, sealing, power, fluid power, control, cameras and lasers.

parts.name: Competition Rules
parts.blurb: Roles and timing at the pool, how a run is scored, and building for the real venue.

parts.name: Engineering and Communication
parts.blurb: The spec sheet, technical documentation, presentation, marketing display and corporate responsibility.

parts.name: Documentation
parts.blurb: The documents to submit and bring, and the deadlines.

parts.name: Props
parts.blurb: Building the mission props so the team can practice the tasks. In the manual this sits at the end of Part 1; it is its own item here because it is real engineering work.

parts.name: Leadership
parts.blurb: Not a section of the manual. It runs through the start-up framing, with titles such as CEO and CFO, and through the scored organizational effectiveness of Navigator and Ranger teams.
